Episode 249. The First Deployment of the Plutonian (10)
Zheung-!
Sigmund, swung like a whip, struck Luke's side. Luke barely managed to block it with his sword, but he was thrust into the debris of the collapsed statue.
Guagh! Luke spat out the hot blood rising in his throat and hastily shifted his gaze. He saw Ban slowly approaching, as if there was no need to hurry.
She was already confident of her victory.
To be precise, she was confident even before the fight began. By Ban's standards, Luke was just an ordinary enemy.

Genesis, though he may be, his will had been twisted long ago, and though he was a Battle God, his sword was outdated. To Ban, the current Luke was an easier opponent than the Battle Kings brothers or the superhumans of the alliance.
"You, who don't even know what the Plutonian is… Who are you to teach others?"
Luke glared at Ban and said.

"As we're cornered, do you have to spout such desperate nonsense? It's getting worse, Luke. Honestly, I hope I can find something to acknowledge in you before I kill you. I want to think less of the ancestors who believed in you."
It was sincere. However, Luke continued with a story completely different from Ban's expectations.
"Ban, our Plutonian is fundamentally a race blessed by the Sun God."
"So?"
"It means we originally owe a debt to the Sun God,Kinzelo. Do you think that power you have... is entirely the result of your own efforts?"
Ban first unleashed another bolt of lightning before answering. Debris from the statue scattered, raising a thick cloud of dust. Luke fended off the subsequent lightning and steadied his stance.

"You have received the most blessings among the Plutonian. Your successor, Jin Runkandel, is the same... Even if I fall today, in the end, you'll move according to the blessing and will left by the Sun God."
At that, Ban blinked at Luke for a while, then suddenly burst into laughter, bending at the waist.
"Hahaha…! A masterpiece, truly."
Luke, seeing Ban laugh unguardedly, couldn't rashly attack. Despite appearances, there were no openings.

"Background, or environment, ultimately dominates everything… In other words, that's what you're saying, Luke. It's true that our Plutonian is inherently stronger in battle compared to other creatures. The hypothesis that it's due to the Sun God's blessing is entirely plausible. But what do you want me to do about it?"
Luke didn't answer and focused his mind, ready to counter Sigmund at any moment.

"Even without the Sun God, everything in this world is born with its own background. Some overcome life's unfairness, while others, born wealthy and strong, still resent the world. In the end, what matters is whether you can endure your life or not."
Ban decided not to expect anything from Luke anymore. He was just a bug lost in madness, nothing more, nothing less.

"Whatever the Sun God gave us, we have no intention of being his plaything. We never asked anything from him. I have experienced a great failure in life, and now I am rising again. Unlike you, lost in vain delusions."
"Then let me ask you this. If I have the Sun God, you have Jin Runkandel. Ultimately, aren't you achieving things with Jin Runkandel's help, things you couldn't overcome with your own will?"
"Such a pitifully weak argument. But to answer you... How can relying on another person and relying on a fanciful being be the same? They're fundamentally different realms."
The conversation ended.
Ban, with a now humorless expression, had cold, hard eyes. Luke sensed his own death.
By now, the priestess must have realized that the first temple was under attack, but sending reinforcements was pointless.
The military power of the Sun God religion was focused on Luke alone. The resurrected ancient heroes were no match for Ban and the Tuwang.
'Is all that's left to pray that the priestess safely hides with the followers…’
With the speed of light.
Sigmund fell above Luke's forehead. This time, Luke reacted perfectly and was able to strike with his great sword.
“Cough...!”

However, the moment the swords clashed, Luke spewed blood from every orifice on his face. And behind him, a vast trail of sword marks was left across the entire void, spanning the sanctuary and the first temple.
A concentrated strike with the Plutonian Domination Sword.
Even Luke, who had ascended to Genesis, could not fathom the destructive power condensed into a small object called a blade and a single vertical cut.
Unavoidable even if known, and irreparable even if blocked. Even for someone like Genesis.
With overwhelming pressure, one of his knees buckled. Luke, trembling from the effort of exerting his strength, barely managed to stop Sigmund.
The lightning that spanned the void continuously formed shockwaves. Behind Luke, not a single intact object remained; everything was destroyed.
The space itself distorted into hundreds of strange whirlpools, and the debris of the first temple was continuously sucked into them.
“Huff, ck!”
On the other hand, Ban's hands holding the sword didn't even twitch. She just sternly, overwhelmingly dominated Luke.
Then Ban struck down with Sigmund once more. In that moment, Luke managed to stand up again and strike with his sword, only to immediately collapse again.
The sound of his kneecap shattering was heard. Inside his clenched mouth, his molars broke, and it felt as though his brain was bouncing around in his head.
His vision flickered on and off rapidly. Luke tried to concentrate and read Ban's movements, but she was still not in a hurry.
She didn't even attempt to attack in Luke's blurred vision, nor did she take advantage of his faltering stance.
There was no need for her to.
"You are a disgrace to the Plutonian."
Kwaang-!
The third strike fell on Luke's great sword. His knees were already shattered, and it seemed like his spine would soon collapse.
A will transcending the flesh, a fighting spirit surpassing death.
It was then that Luke realized. He had forgotten such things long ago. That's why his broken legs wouldn't move, and he couldn't fight as usual.
He was trapped in a limit. The limit of faith as a Sun God religion. Therefore, the fact that he had ascended to Genesis in the distant past had become a meaningless story from that moment.
Sigmund continued to strike down.
The battle had already become more of a one-sided act of violence than a fight. Ban's emotionless face as she wielded her sword made her seem not like a person, but like merciless punishment itself.
"Huh, still breathing, and you've dropped your sword?"
After finishing the twenty-sixth vertical cut, Ban paused briefly and opened her mouth as if in disbelief.

Luke was breathing harshly, like the grating sound of metal. Barely alive, his face was unrecognizable. The arm that had been cut at the shoulder had fallen off somewhere, and only above the knees of his legs remained.
His radiant heart was shattered like a broken watermelon, and the essence of the Sun God that he had harbored before the battle was flowing out through the cracks.
That's when he had just dropped his great sword.
"Kinzelo will… find you…"
"Good, I'm glad you're seeking the Sun God till the end. If you suddenly found the brothers you abandoned at this moment, I would have been so disgusted that I couldn't sleep tonight."
The energy of the Plutonian Domination Sword was converging into Ban's radiant heart. After a moment of steadying that energy, Ban raised her sword for the last time.
Then she immediately stabbed Luke's radiant heart. The blade, squeezing through the cracks, rotated violently once, and Luke met his end.
The Sun energy flowing out of the radiant heart slowly gathered in the air. Ban, feeling disgusted, was about to cut off that energy with her sword but then stopped.
She needed to observe what the Sun energy was trying to do, where it was heading. If it tried to leave the void and go elsewhere, that place was likely another stronghold of the Sun God religion.
"You've done well, Battle God brothers."
The Battle Kings brothers approached Ban.
They were disappointed. It was obvious that Ban would win, but the fact that someone who was once a Battle God didn't even properly counterattack before dying was unbelievable.
"Hmm, isn't he weaker than the Battle Kings present here?"

"That's right. Although in martial prowess Luke may have been superior, any of the brothers would have been able to defeat him. He confined himself within his own limits... When we return, tell all the brothers not to forget this pathetic end."
"Understood."
Ban alternately looked at the Sun energy, now transformed into a sphere, and the priests she had spared earlier. The priests were still looking for Kinzelo.
Ban laid a hand on one of them.
"You're not dead like the others next to you. And you don't smell of blood."
"Yes… I mean, I, I am."
"From now on, if you tell us how to get to another stronghold of the Sun God religion, I will give you a chance. A chance to break away from this cult and live a proper life."
"In this rotten world, there's nothing that can compensate us… Cough."
Another priest shouted in his place, but Kaio lightly flicked his finger, turning his jaw. He lost consciousness, his face twisted.

"Of course, as Jin brother said in his speech, there will be proper legal proceedings. If you haven't committed any serious crimes like murder or something equivalent since joining the Sun God religion, you can have a fresh start."
"Priest, no, don't."
"Ah."
The other two priests classified as dead by Ban also lost consciousness.
"What will you do?"
The remaining priest, trembling, looked back and forth between the fallen priests and Ban. Even the gruesome corpse of Luke was in front of him, making him feel his faith wavering for the first time.
Even if he didn't help, from Ban's perspective, it was enough to just take the priests to Valeria. The priest also knew this well.
"I'll... help as much as I can, with what I know. First, there's a path here that leads to the second temple. If it hasn't been destroyed..."
Ban nodded, seemingly satisfied.
"Lead the way. We leave immediately."
